blocks.text: Use a structured pipeline: intent capture -> proposal adapter -> evidence and capability validation -> review store -> versioned action coordinator -> per-item outcome reducer. Generated content never bypasses review or product permissions.

ProposalAdapter validates structured, escaped proposal data. ReviewStore owns selection and edits. CapabilityGate derives allowed actions from evidence freshness and permissions. ActionCoordinator submits one idempotent versioned command and reconciles per-item outcomes.

Boundary checks:
- Proposal is separate from user decision.
- Evidence and capabilities have explicit freshness.
- Local review edits survive safe proposal refreshes.
- Pending command overlays rather than rewrites authority.
- Outcomes retain item-level success, failure, and recovery.

blocks.title: Core building blocks
rows: ProposalAdapter
Validates structured generated content
Treats model output as untrusted data.
ReviewStore
Owns selected items, edits, acknowledgement, and focus context
Keeps user intent inspectable and reversible.
CapabilityGate
Combines proposal version, evidence freshness, and permission
Display text never grants authority.
ActionCoordinator
Submits idempotent command and merges per-item results
Optimism cannot fabricate complete success.

blocks.code:
Intent capture
  -> ProposalAdapter (validate and escape)
  -> Proposal cache (identity + version + evidence freshness)
  -> CapabilityGate
  -> ReviewStore (selection + edits)
  -> ActionCoordinator (command ID + version precondition)
  -> Outcome reducer (per-item authoritative result)
  -> Review panel, status summary, and focused recovery

blocks.title: Proposal authority and action decisions
items: Proposal, review, command, and outcome have separate owners.
Cancel stops local waiting; it does not claim remote work stopped.
Confirmation revalidates proposal version and capability.
Retry keeps the same command identity only when the contract is idempotent.

blocks.title: Unsafe proposal and action coupling
items: Treating generated prose as an executable command.
Replacing per-item outcomes with one success banner.
Rendering generated markup without an allowlisted formatter.

steps.title: 1. Request
steps.text: Capture intent under a request identity and keep pending work cancellable.

steps.title: 2. Review
steps.text: Validate proposal structure, show evidence and limitations, and derive capabilities.

steps.title: 3. Confirm
steps.text: Snapshot reviewed item IDs and edits under one versioned idempotent command.

steps.title: 4. Reconcile
steps.text: Merge per-item outcomes, focus the first recoverable failure, and preserve successful evidence.

items.label: Capability
items.helperText: Freshness and permission determine allowed actions.

blocks.title: Proposal and action ownership
blocks.text: AI UX reliability comes from separating generated advice, user review, product capability, command intent, and authoritative outcomes.
Worked example: uncertain suggestion affects a destructive edit

An assistant proposes removing three records but reports incomplete evidence. The UI must not convert a probabilistic suggestion into an automatic destructive command or hide which records were inferred.

blocks.title: Scenario walkthrough
rows: Suggestion arrives

Render a review state rather than completed success.
Suggestion is not an action.
Evidence is incomplete
Mark unsupported records and disable bulk confirmation.
Explain what needs review in plain language.
Uncertainty changes interaction.
User edits selection
Create explicit local intent containing only reviewed records.
Preview shows the exact effect and undo policy.
User authority is inspectable.
Command resolves
Merge authoritative per-record outcomes and retain failures.
Show partial success with focused recovery.
